chunks: First: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Adam ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fi, who said: I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a letter from Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik arrived concerning a man who dug up a woman, stripped her of her clothes, and married her. The people had differed regarding us on this matter; one group said 'Kill him' and another group said 'Burn him'. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'The sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living, his punishment is one hundred (lashes).'

Second: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding the one who comes to the woman while she is dead, he said: 'Her burden (of sin) is greater than the one who comes to her while she is alive.'

Third: And what Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Sulayman ibn Dawud, from al-Nu'man ibn Abd al-Salam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I asked him about a man who committed fornication with a dead woman, he said: 'There is no fixed punishment (hadd) upon him.'

This report carries two meanings: One is that the intended meaning is that there is no specific fixed punishment (hadd) upon him, and no other ruling is permissible, because we have clarified in the first report that chastity (ihsan) and its lack are considered therein; if he were chaste, the punishment would be stoning, and if not chaste, his punishment would be one hundred lashes, and this is not on a single level ground. The other meaning is that the report is specific to one who came to his own wife after her death, for the full punishment is not established upon him and he is given discretionary punishment (ta'zir) as the Imam sees fit.

key_terms.إِحْصَان: Chastity or being in a state of marital fidelity (affecting punishment)
key_terms.نَبَشَ: To dig up or unearth (specifically a grave)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a man who has intercourse with a dead woman?
ai.summary: This passage from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the jurisprudential debate among Shia scholars regarding *Baj' al-Mawta* (sexual intercourse with a corpse), specifically contrasting the view that the dead's sanctity mirrors the living with the opinion that the fixed *hadd* does not apply. It distinguishes between a stranger and one's own wife, noting that while the former may incur the full penalty, the latter is subject to discretionary *ta'zir* by the Imam, reflecting the nuance in applying *Ihsan* (marital status) to the deceased. This discussion underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of legal personhood and honor (*Hurmat*) after death.
